paper.title: Contextual Thompson Sampling via Generation of Missing Data

settings.name_in_paper: Meta-contextual bandit problem (perfectly calibrated imputation model p*)
unmapped: Task tau = (Z, X_{1:T}, potential outcomes) drawn from an arbitrary joint task distribution p*; contexts and outcomes need not be i.i.d. over time (nonstationary/correlated allowed)
Prior task information Z_tau observed at start of task
Regret measured against best-fitting policy pi*(.;tau) in a designer-chosen policy class Pi (fitted in hindsight on complete data)
Learner knows the true task distribution p* (used as imputation model)
settings.definition_quote: Let bandit tasks $\tau$ be sampled from an unknown distribution $p^*$ ... For each timestep $t \in [1 \colon T]$, the agent observes context $X_t$, selects action $A_t \in \MC{A}_{\tau}$, observes outcome $Y_t = Y_t^{(A_t)}$, and computes reward $R(Y_t)$, for a fixed, known function $R$ in $[0,1]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Meta-contextual bandit problem (approximate imputation model p_theta)
unmapped: Task tau = (Z, X_{1:T}, potential outcomes) drawn from an arbitrary joint task distribution p*; contexts and outcomes need not be i.i.d. over time
Prior task information Z_tau observed at start of task
Regret measured against best-fitting policy in designer-chosen policy class Pi
Learner uses a (possibly misspecified) generative model p_theta learned offline instead of p*
settings.definition_quote: We now present a regret bound for generative TS with an approximate generative model $p_\theta$. The result is notable because $p_\theta$ only affects the regret bound through its offline prediction loss

symbols.H_pi: conditional entropy H(pi*(X_{1:T}) | Z_tau) of the best-fitting policy evaluated at contexts X_{1:T}; O(d log(T K)) for Natarajan dimension d (Prop. 2)

conditions: reward function R takes values in [0,1]

source.label: thm:psarRegretPerfect
source.quote: For Algorithm \ref{alg:Thompson} with imputation model $p^*$, $\mathbb{A}_{\rm{TS-Gen}}(p^*)$, \Delta( \mathbb{A}_{\rm{TS-Gen}}(p^*) ) \leq \sqrt{ \frac{|\MC{A}_\tau|}{2 T} \cdot H ( \piX \mid Z_{\tau} ) }.

results.notes: Paper bounds per-period regret; multiplied by T. Regret averaged over tasks from p* (Bayesian). Combined with Prop. 2, H_pi = O(d log(TK)).

symbols.Gamma_bar: almost-sure upper bound on the information ratio Gamma_t over all t

conditions: reward function R takes values in [0,1]

source.label: thm:psarRegretPerfect
source.quote: Moreover, $\Delta( \mathbb{A}_{\rm{TS-Gen}}(p^*) ) \leq \sqrt{ \frac{\bar{\Gamma}}{T} \cdot H ( \piX \mid Z_{\tau} ) }$, where $\bar{\Gamma}$ bounds the information ratio

symbols.ell_theta: population offline log-loss ell(p_theta) of the imputation model
symbols.ell_star: population offline log-loss ell(p*) of the true task distribution

conditions: reward function R takes values in [0,1]

source.label: thm:psarRegret
source.quote: For Algorithm \ref{alg:Thompson} with imputation model $p_\theta$, $\mathbb{A}_{\rm{TS-Gen}}(p_\theta)$, \Delta \big( \psar(p_\theta) \big) \leq \sqrt{ \frac{|\MC{A}_{\tau}|}{2 T} \cdot H ( \piX \mid Z_\tau ) } + \sqrt{ 2 \{ \ell(p_\theta) - \ell(p^*) \} }.

results.notes: Per-period regret multiplied by T. Expectation over tasks from p*.
